**Step 1: Find the relevant information**

The first memory item is the only one about this paper. It comes from our earlier conversation (recorded 2023-05-22) where I summarized the "Experimental Results" section of the submission. That summary said:

- The HAMLET framework was tested on the OnDA benchmarks and the SHIFT dataset.
- It gave "an average improvement in framerate of approximately 20% when using the Hardware-Aware Modular Training (HAMT) agent."
- Adding the Active Training Modulation system gave "a further improvement of approximately 4x."

The other two memory items (one on MPC/LSTM control papers, one on autocross) are not related to this question.

**Step 2: Work out the answer**

The question asks only about the HAMT agent, so the figure you need is the ~20% framerate gain. The ~4x gain is a separate, additional improvement that comes from the Active Training Modulation system.

**Answer:**

Using the HAMT agent gave an **average framerate improvement of about 20%**. Adding the Active Training Modulation system on top of HAMT brought a further improvement of about 4x.
